summary: Family seal maker (45 staff, EUR 22.9 M); we are only 0.2 % of its turnover and it is reviewing small accounts. Owner offered an open-book walk-through. Supplies O-ring sets and half the lip seals (EUR 100.98/100, 9.6 % below Pirkheim) and is qualified on the casing gasket. Our kit plan (about 25 000 kits a year) would roughly triple its business with us: trade the kit for price. Open deep.
notes: Wants volume, fears being a small, unprofitable account; the kit consolidation answers both. Gave way historically (kept 18 % of asks) but took +2.4-2.6 % last year. Fast 7-day lead time, green scorecard (OTD 92 %) yet 39 complaints in 3 years. Payment record fine (2.8 days late).
fears: being dropped as a small account

evidence.quote: they are reviewing small accounts and will focus on customers with volume.
he offered to walk us through their calculation (hourly rates and material) if that helps to settle prices.

levers: whole kit: O-ring sets, casing gasket and lip seals (about 25 000 kits a year)
arguments: kit volume: one supplier for 2 O-ring sets, 1 gasket, 2 lip seals per kit
binding volume commitment with schedule CSV
its own cost shares from the offered open-book walk-through
elastomer/material index, only if it actually fell
avoid: citing a cost driver that rose
presenting us as a small one-part buyer
tactics: Open deep and put the kit on the table early: it turns a small account into a volume customer.
Offer a binding annual kit volume and send the volume schedule.
Ask for the hourly-rate and material breakdown it offered and argue from its cost shares.
Trade 100 % lip-seal quota (taken from sup:70440) for the price step.
Move in small visible steps, one argument kind per round.
playbook.expected_concession: No arena data; history: settled 0 % on most asks but took +2.4-2.6 % last year; volume should buy a real step.
